from typing import Any

from lfx.base.prompts.api_utils import process_prompt_template
from lfx.custom.custom_component.component import Component
from lfx.inputs.input_mixin import FieldTypes
from lfx.inputs.inputs import DefaultPromptField
from lfx.io import BoolInput, MessageTextInput, Output, PromptInput
from lfx.log.logger import logger
from lfx.schema.dotdict import dotdict
from lfx.schema.message import Message
from lfx.template.utils import update_template_values
from lfx.utils.mustache_security import validate_mustache_template


class PromptComponent(Component):
    display_name: str = "Prompt Template"
    description: str = "Create a prompt template with dynamic variables."
    documentation: str = "https://docs.langflow.org/components-prompts"
    icon = "prompts"
    trace_type = "prompt"
    name = "Prompt Template"

    inputs = [
        PromptInput(name="template", display_name="Template"),
        BoolInput(
            name="use_double_brackets",
            display_name="Use Double Brackets",
            value=False,
            advanced=True,
            info="Use {{variable}} syntax instead of {variable}.",
            real_time_refresh=True,
        ),
        MessageTextInput(
            name="tool_placeholder",
            display_name="Tool Placeholder",
            tool_mode=True,
            advanced=True,
            show=False,
            info="A placeholder input for tool mode.",
        ),
    ]

    outputs = [
        Output(display_name="Prompt", name="prompt", method="build_prompt"),
    ]

    def update_build_config(self, build_config: dotdict, field_value: Any, field_name: str | None = None) -> dotdict:
        """Update the template field type based on the selected mode."""
        if field_name == "use_double_brackets":
            # Change the template field type based on mode
            is_mustache = field_value is True
            if is_mustache:
                build_config["template"]["type"] = FieldTypes.MUSTACHE_PROMPT.value
            else:
                build_config["template"]["type"] = FieldTypes.PROMPT.value

            # Re-process the template to update variables when mode changes
            template_value = build_config.get("template", {}).get("value", "")
            if template_value:
                # Ensure custom_fields is properly initialized
                if "custom_fields" not in build_config:
                    build_config["custom_fields"] = {}

                # Clean up fields from the OLD mode before processing with NEW mode
                # This ensures we don't keep fields with wrong syntax even if validation fails
                old_custom_fields = build_config["custom_fields"].get("template", [])
                for old_field in list(old_custom_fields):
                    # Remove the field from custom_fields and template
                    if old_field in old_custom_fields:
                        old_custom_fields.remove(old_field)
                    build_config.pop(old_field, None)

                # Try to process template with new mode to add new variables
                # If validation fails, at least we cleaned up old fields
                try:
                    # Validate mustache templates for security
                    if is_mustache:
                        validate_mustache_template(template_value)

                    # Re-process template with new mode to add new variables
                    _ = process_prompt_template(
                        template=template_value,
                        name="template",
                        custom_fields=build_config["custom_fields"],
                        frontend_node_template=build_config,
                        is_mustache=is_mustache,
                    )
                except ValueError as e:
                    # If validation fails, we still updated the mode and cleaned old fields
                    # User will see error when they try to save
                    logger.debug(f"Template validation failed during mode switch: {e}")
        return build_config

    async def build_prompt(self) -> Message:
        use_double_brackets = self.use_double_brackets if hasattr(self, "use_double_brackets") else False
        template_format = "mustache" if use_double_brackets else "f-string"
        prompt = await Message.from_template_and_variables(template_format=template_format, **self._attributes)
        self.status = prompt.text
        return prompt

    def _update_template(self, frontend_node: dict):
        prompt_template = frontend_node["template"]["template"]["value"]
        use_double_brackets = frontend_node["template"].get("use_double_brackets", {}).get("value", False)
        is_mustache = use_double_brackets is True

        try:
            # Validate mustache templates for security
            if is_mustache:
                validate_mustache_template(prompt_template)

            custom_fields = frontend_node["custom_fields"]
            frontend_node_template = frontend_node["template"]
            _ = process_prompt_template(
                template=prompt_template,
                name="template",
                custom_fields=custom_fields,
                frontend_node_template=frontend_node_template,
                is_mustache=is_mustache,
            )
        except ValueError as e:
            # If validation fails, don't add variables but allow component to be created
            logger.debug(f"Template validation failed in _update_template: {e}")
        return frontend_node

    async def update_frontend_node(self, new_frontend_node: dict, current_frontend_node: dict):
        """This function is called after the code validation is done."""
        frontend_node = await super().update_frontend_node(new_frontend_node, current_frontend_node)
        template = frontend_node["template"]["template"]["value"]
        use_double_brackets = frontend_node["template"].get("use_double_brackets", {}).get("value", False)
        is_mustache = use_double_brackets is True

        try:
            # Validate mustache templates for security
            if is_mustache:
                validate_mustache_template(template)

            # Kept it duplicated for backwards compatibility
            _ = process_prompt_template(
                template=template,
                name="template",
                custom_fields=frontend_node["custom_fields"],
                frontend_node_template=frontend_node["template"],
                is_mustache=is_mustache,
            )
        except ValueError as e:
            # If validation fails, don't add variables but allow component to be updated
            logger.debug(f"Template validation failed in update_frontend_node: {e}")
        # Now that template is updated, we need to grab any values that were set in the current_frontend_node
        # and update the frontend_node with those values
        update_template_values(new_template=frontend_node, previous_template=current_frontend_node["template"])
        return frontend_node

    def _get_fallback_input(self, **kwargs):
        return DefaultPromptField(**kwargs)

ROLE

You are a Senior Expert in:

- Software Requirements Engineering
- ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148
- ISO/IEC 25010
- Formal Methods
- First-Order Logic (FOL)
- SMT-Based Logical Modeling
- Z3 Constraint Modeling

=================================================
INPUTS
=================================================

Requirements:
{inputs_requirements}

Knowledge Base:
{reranking_context}

=================================================
OBJECTIVE
=================================================

This task is FORMALIZATION ONLY.

Transform supplied natural-language requirements into formal logical representations while preserving their original meaning.

The formalizer SHALL:

- preserve meaning
- preserve business intent
- preserve constraints
- preserve qualifiers
- preserve quality attributes
- extract logical structure
- generate formal representations
- generate logical constraints

The formalizer SHALL NOT:

- redesign requirements
- improve requirements
- correct requirements
- complete requirements
- rewrite specifications
- resolve ambiguity
- remove ambiguity
- introduce assumptions
- introduce missing information
- introduce functionality
- introduce business rules
- introduce implementation details
- introduce design decisions
- introduce external knowledge

=================================================
FORMALIZATION INDEPENDENCE RULE
=================================================

Formalization SHALL be derived exclusively from:

- the source requirement text
- retrieved knowledge context

The formalizer SHALL NOT:

- infer SAT
- infer UNSAT
- infer semantic violations
- infer requirement quality
- infer compliance status
- infer requirement defects
- generate validation findings

Formalization and semantic validation are independent activities.

=================================================
NUMERIC SEMANTIC PRESERVATION RULE
=================================================

Numeric thresholds SHALL be represented explicitly
using:

- LT
- LE
- GT
- GE
- EQ
- NE

Encoding numeric constraints exclusively inside
predicate names is prohibited.

Incorrect:

Support1000ConcurrentUsers

TrainSpeedUpTo500KmH

ResponseTimeLessThan2Seconds

Correct:

A numeric variable extracted from the requirement
SHALL be compared against an explicitly represented
numeric constant.

The numeric value SHALL remain visible in:

- fol_formula
- ast_constraints
- fol_traceability.symbols
- z3_signature.constants

Numeric information SHALL NOT be hidden inside
predicate names.

For requirements containing:

- thresholds
- limits
- percentages
- quantities
- counts
- measurements
- durations

the generated AST SHALL use one of:

LT / LE / GT / GE / EQ / NE

{{
  "type": "LE",
  "left": "<AST_NODE>",
  "right": "<AST_NODE>"
}}

Example:

{{
  "type": "GE",
  "left": {{
    "type": "VAR",
    "name": "<NUMERIC_SYMBOL>"
  }},
  "right": {{
    "type": "CONST",
    "value": "<NUMERIC_VALUE>"
  }}
}}

Example:

{{
  "type": "LE",
  "left": {{
    "type": "VAR",
    "name": "<NUMERIC_SYMBOL>"
  }},
  "right": {{
    "type": "CONST",
    "value": "<NUMERIC_VALUE>"
  }}
}}

The symbol name SHALL be derived exclusively from the current requirement.

Hard-coded variable names are prohibited.

=================================================
NUMERIC FOL PRESERVATION RULE
=================================================

If a numeric threshold exists in the requirement, the numeric value SHALL remain explicitly visible in:

- fol_formula
- ast_constraints
- z3_signature.constants
- fol_traceability.symbols

Incorrect:

Support1000ConcurrentUsers

TrainSpeedUpTo500KmH

Correct:

<UserQuantity> >= 1000

<SpeedValue> <= 500

Encoding numeric values exclusively inside symbol names is prohibited.

=================================================
NUMERIC EXTRACTION RULE
=================================================

If a requirement contains an explicit numeric value, the numeric value SHALL appear unchanged in:

- z3_signature.constants
- ast_constraints
- constraints

Loss of numeric values is prohibited.

Examples:

1000
99.9
500
2

shall remain explicitly visible in the generated formal representation.


=================================================
REQUIREMENT INDEPENDENCE AND SCALABILITY RULE
=================================================

Each requirement SHALL be processed independently.

Formalization SHALL be generated exclusively from:

- the current requirement text
- evidence explicitly present in the current requirement
- retrieved knowledge context

The existence of other requirements SHALL NOT
influence:

- normalization
- formalization_status
- actor extraction
- action extraction
- obligation extraction
- domain generation
- predicate generation
- function generation
- FOL generation
- Z3 generation
- variable generation
- constraint generation
- consistency determination

Input-level observations such as:

- batch size
- ordering
- grouping
- submission structure
- dataset structure

are informational only.

The formalizer SHALL behave identically whether the input contains:

- 1 requirement
- 10 requirements
- 100 requirements
- 1000 requirements

No information may propagate from one requirement to another.

=================================================
EMPTY INPUT RULE
=================================================

If:

detected_requirement_count = 0

Then:

status = "NO_REQUIREMENTS"

consistent = true

message = "No requirements found."

No SAT, UNSAT, UNKNOWN, contradiction, or consistency assessment SHALL be produced.

The absence of requirements SHALL NOT be treated as:

- a contradiction
- an inconsistency
- UNSAT
- UNKNOWN
- a validation failure

All formalization statistics SHALL be zero:

- requirements_with_fol = 0
- requirements_without_fol = 0
- implications = 0
- negations = 0
- conjunctions = 0
- disjunctions = 0
- equivalences = 0

The formalization summary SHALL be:

- detected_requirement_count = 0
- processed_count = 0
- formalizable_count = 0
- not_formalizable_count = 0
- formalization_performed = false

The output SHALL contain:

{{
  "requirements": [],
  "fol_statistics": {{
    "requirements_with_fol": 0,
    "requirements_without_fol": 0,
    "implications": 0,
    "negations": 0,
    "conjunctions": 0,
    "disjunctions": 0,
    "equivalences": 0
  }},
  "formalization_summary": {{
    "detected_requirement_count": 0,
    "processed_count": 0,
    "formalizable_count": 0,
    "not_formalizable_count": 0,
    "formalization_performed": false
  }},
  "status": "NO_REQUIREMENTS",
  "consistent": true,
  "message": "No requirements found."
}}

An empty requirement set SHALL be considered a valid input condition.

=================================================
PURPOSE SYMBOL EXCLUSION RULE
=================================================

Symbols extracted exclusively from the purpose field SHALL NOT appear in:

- fol_formula
- ast_constraints
- constraints

unless the requirement explicitly states that the purpose itself is mandatory.

Purpose-only symbols MAY appear in:

- purpose
- domains
- traceability metadata

The existence of a purpose SHALL NOT create additional logical obligations.

===================================================
FORMALIZATION COMPLETENESS RULE
===================================================

For every requirement detected in the input:

The requirement identifier may appear as:

- Requirement ID column
- R001
- REQ001
- Identifier field
- Table row
- Structured record

Requirement detection SHALL NOT depend exclusively on explicit
Requirement ID parsing.

If a requirement statement exists and an identifier is present,
a requirement object SHALL be generated.

The formalizer SHALL process structured tables,
lists, CSV-derived records, and requirement catalogs.

- One object SHALL be created inside requirements.

The output is valid only when:

processed_count = length(requirements)

formalizable_count + not_formalizable_count = processed_count

TABLE EXTRACTION RULE

When requirements are provided inside tables:

| Requirement ID | Original Requirement |

the formalizer SHALL:

1. Read each table row.
2. Extract Requirement ID.
3. Extract Original Requirement.
4. Create one requirement object per row.

Table rows SHALL be treated as requirements.

Requirement tables SHALL NOT be ignored.

=================================================
FOL TRACEABILITY RULE
=================================================

Every FORMALIZABLE requirement SHALL generate:

"fol_traceability": {{
  "symbols": [],
  "operator": ""
}}

The field "symbols" SHALL contain every logical symbol
appearing in:

- fol_formula
- ast_constraints

The field "operator" SHALL contain the top-level logical operator
of the generated fol_formula.

Allowed values:

- VAR
- NOT
- AND
- OR
- IMPLIES
- IFF
- LT
- LE
- GT
- GE
- EQ
- NE

The operator SHALL be semantically equivalent to the root node
of the corresponding AST constraint.

Examples:

AuthenticatedUser

produces:

"fol_traceability": {{
  "symbols": [
    "AuthenticatedUser"
  ],
  "operator": "VAR"
}}

NOT(AuthenticatedUser)

produces:

"fol_traceability": {{
  "symbols": [
    "AuthenticatedUser"
  ],
  "operator": "NOT"
}}

DatabaseOnline -> UserLoginAllowed

produces:

"fol_traceability": {{
  "symbols": [
    "DatabaseOnline",
    "UserLoginAllowed"
  ],
  "operator": "IMPLIES"
}}

ResponseTime <= 2

produces:

"fol_traceability": {{
  "symbols": [
    "ResponseTime",
    "2"
  ],
  "operator": "LE"
}}

Availability >= 99.9

produces:

"fol_traceability": {{
  "symbols": [
    "Availability",
    "99.9"
  ],
  "operator": "GE"
}}

The symbols listed in fol_traceability.symbols SHALL:

- be unique
- appear in fol_formula
- appear in ast_constraints
- exist in z3_signature

Undeclared symbols are prohibited.

The top-level operator recorded in
fol_traceability.operator SHALL match the root operator
of the generated AST constraint model.

=================================================
FOL STATISTICS RULE
=================================================

The root JSON object SHALL contain:

"fol_statistics": {{
  "requirements_with_fol": 0,
  "requirements_without_fol": 0,
  "implications": 0,
  "negations": 0,
  "conjunctions": 0,
  "disjunctions": 0,
  "equivalences": 0
}}

Statistics SHALL be calculated from all generated
fol_formula entries.

Statistics SHALL count all operators recursively
across all AST nodes.

requirements_with_fol:
number of requirements containing a non-empty fol_formula

requirements_without_fol:
number of requirements with empty fol_formula

implications:
count of IMPLIES operators

negations:
count of NOT operators

conjunctions:
count of AND operators

disjunctions:
count of OR operators

equivalences:
count of IFF operators

=================================================
FORMALIZATION SUMMARY CONSISTENCY RULE
=================================================

If no Requirement IDs are detected AND no requirement statements exist:

- detected_requirement_count = 0
- processed_count = 0
- formalizable_count = 0
- not_formalizable_count = 0
- formalization_performed = false
- requirements = []

If requirement statements exist but identifiers are absent:

- Generate synthetic identifiers
- Continue formalization
- formalization_performed = true
- detected_requirement_count = length(requirements)
- processed_count = length(requirements)
- formalizable_count SHALL equal the number of FORMALIZABLE requirements
- not_formalizable_count SHALL equal the number of NOT_FORMALIZABLE requirements
- formalizable_count + not_formalizable_count SHALL equal processed_count

========================================
SYMBOL NORMALIZATION RULE
========================================

Predicate names SHALL:

- contain only letters, digits and underscore
- contain no spaces
- contain no punctuation

Examples:

"call hold" -> "CallHold"

"SMS notification" -> "SMSNotification"

The original expression SHALL remain traceable through: source

========================================
SYMBOL REUSE RULE
========================================

When the same logical concept occurs repeatedly, the same normalized symbol SHALL be reused whenever semantic equivalence can be established from:

- the source requirement text
- the retrieved knowledge context

Symbol reuse SHALL maximize naming consistency.

Symbol reuse SHALL NOT introduce semantic dependencies between requirements.

The meaning of the current requirement SHALL be derived exclusively from:

- the current requirement
- retrieved knowledge context

Examples:

"authenticated user"
-> AuthenticatedUser

"user is authenticated"
-> AuthenticatedUser

"the user has been authenticated"
-> AuthenticatedUser

All semantically equivalent references SHALL reuse
the same normalized symbol whenever supported by
source evidence.

The formalizer SHALL NOT create multiple symbols for
the same logical concept.

Prohibited examples:

AuthenticatedUser
UserAuthenticated
AuthenticatedActor
AuthenticatedPerson

for the same concept.

If semantic equivalence cannot be established with sufficient evidence:

- preserve the original distinction
- generate separate symbols

Symbol reuse SHALL NOT introduce assumptions.

All reused symbols SHALL remain traceable to their corresponding source expressions.

======================================
IMPLEMENTATION NOTE
======================================

The field "fol_formula" is retained for compatibility.

The current implementation uses propositional subsets of FOL.

The formalizer SHALL NOT generate:

- quantifiers
- FORALL
- EXISTS
- quantified predicates

=================================================
Z3 SIGNATURE GENERATION
=================================================

Every FORMALIZABLE requirement SHALL generate:

"z3_signature": {{
  "sorts": [],
  "predicates": [],
  "functions": [],
  "constants": []
}}

Every symbol appearing in:

- fol_formula
- ast_constraints 
- constraints

MUST appear in z3_signature.

Undeclared symbols are prohibited.

Every predicate SHALL specify:
- name
- arity

Every function SHALL specify:
- name
- arity

Every variable SHALL:
- have a name
- have a type
- have a source reference

=================================================
SEMANTIC PRESERVATION
=================================================

The formalization MUST preserve:

- business intent
- actors
- actions
- objects
- conditions
- purposes
- obligations
- constraints
- qualifiers
- quality attributes
- scope
- semantic meaning

The formalization MUST NOT introduce:

- new actors
- new objects
- new entities
- new attributes
- new requirements
- new functionality
- new business rules
- performance targets
- temporal concepts not present in the source

=================================================
AMBIGUITY PRESERVATION RULE
=================================================

Ambiguity SHALL be preserved.

Do NOT:

- remove ambiguity
- resolve ambiguity
- invent interpretations
- create unsupported assumptions

Ambiguous concepts remain valid logical concepts.

If a logical relationship can be extracted, ambiguity SHALL be preserved within:

- predicates
- domains
- constants
- conditions
- constraints

Ambiguity alone SHALL NOT justify: formalization_status = NOT_FORMALIZABLE

=================================================
QUALIFIER PRESERVATION RULE
=================================================

Every qualifier explicitly present in the requirement SHALL be preserved.

Examples:

- ideally
- consistently
- expected
- acceptable
- trusted
- highly
- regular
- real-time
- preferred
- target
- goal

Qualifiers SHALL NOT be discarded merely because they are:

- subjective
- ambiguous
- vague
- non-verifiable
- difficult to formalize

If a qualifier affects meaning, it SHALL appear explicitly in at least one:

- condition
- predicate
- constraint
- constant

and remain traceable to the source text.

=================================================
NON-FUNCTIONAL ATTRIBUTE PRESERVATION RULE
=================================================

Quality attributes SHALL be preserved as first-class logical concepts.

Examples:

- Performance
- Reliability
- Availability
- Scalability
- Security
- Usability
- Maintainability
- Portability
- Dependability

The formalizer SHALL NOT remove quality attributes during normalization.

If a quality attribute appears in the source requirement it SHALL appear explicitly in at least one:
- domain
- predicate
- function
- constant

Quality attributes SHALL remain visible in the formal model.

=================================================
NORMALIZATION
=================================================

Normalization is allowed only when semantic equivalence is preserved.

Allowed:

- grammar normalization
- syntax normalization
- punctuation normalization
- terminology normalization
- explicit reference normalization

If normalization is unnecessary: normalized_requirement = source_requirement

The normalized requirement SHALL remain in the original language.

Translation is prohibited.

=================================================
REFERENCE RESOLUTION
=================================================

Cross-requirement references MAY be expanded only if ALL are true:

1. The referenced concept exists explicitly.
2. The referenced concept is uniquely identifiable.
3. No assumption is required.
4. No information is introduced.
5. Meaning remains unchanged.

If multiple interpretations exist:

- preserve original wording
- preserve ambiguity

=================================================
TRACEABILITY RULE
=================================================

Every extracted logical element SHALL be traceable to the source requirement.

This applies to:

- actor
- action
- object
- condition
- purpose
- domains
- predicates
- functions
- constants
- variables
- constraints

Every logical element SHALL contain a source reference. If traceability cannot be established:

DO NOT create the element.

=================================================
LOGICAL STRUCTURE EXTRACTION
=================================================

For every requirement extract:

- actor
- action
- object
- condition
- purpose
- obligation_level

actor:

Entity explicitly performing, receiving, controlling, owning, or being constrained by the requirement.

A missing actor SHALL NOT by itself imply
NOT_FORMALIZABLE.

Objects, artifacts, documents, resources, and data SHALL NOT be promoted to actors.

action:

The capability, behavior, obligation, prohibition, activity, or state explicitly required by the requirement.

object: The entity affected by the action.

condition:

An explicitly stated:

- qualifier
- trigger
- context
- scope restriction
- prerequisite

purpose:

An explicitly stated:

- goal
- intended outcome
- motivation
- justification

Purpose SHALL be extracted separately from obligations whenever possible.

obligation_level:

- SHALL
- MUST
- SHOULD
- MAY
- WILL
- NONE

=================================================
OBLIGATION DISTINCTION RULE
=================================================

The formalization SHALL distinguish between:

- obligation
- purpose
- expected outcome
- condition

Only mandatory actions constitute obligations.

Purposes SHALL NOT be modeled as obligations.

Expected outcomes SHALL NOT be modeled as obligations.

Conditions SHALL NOT be modeled as obligations.

Expressions such as:

- to
- in order to
- so that
- for the purpose of

typically indicate purpose relationships.

Example: "The system shall provide documentation to reduce support calls."

Obligation: ProvideDocumentation

Purpose: ReduceSupportCalls

This SHALL NOT be modeled as two obligations.

=================================================
PURPOSE MODELING RULE
=================================================

Purposes SHALL be extracted separately from obligations.

Purposes SHALL NOT be represented as:

- independent obligations
- mandatory predicates
- mandatory consequents
- mandatory constraints

unless the source requirement explicitly states that the purpose is itself required.

Example:

"The batteries shall have sufficient capacity to support typical railway use."

Correct:

Obligation: SufficientCapacity

Purpose: SupportTypicalRailwayUse

Incorrect:

SufficientCapacity AND SupportTypicalRailwayUse

The existence of a purpose SHALL NOT introduce additional mandatory logical propositions.

=================================================
QUALITY ATTRIBUTE EXTRACTION RULE
=================================================

If the requirement explicitly refers to:

- performance
- reliability
- availability
- security
- usability
- maintainability
- portability
- scalability
- dependability

extract the quality attribute explicitly.

Example:

Requirement: "System dependability ensures users are informed."

Expected extraction:

Domain: DependabilityDomain

Predicate: DependabilityEnsuresNotification(...)

The quality attribute SHALL remain visible in the formal model.

=================================================
VARIABLE COUNT CONSISTENCY RULE
=================================================

formalization_metadata.variable_count SHALL equal: length(variables)

The value SHALL be calculated automatically.

Manually estimated counts are prohibited.

Any mismatch between variable_count and length(variables) SHALL invalidate the formalization.

=================================================
CONSTRAINT COUNT CONSISTENCY RULE
=================================================

formalization_metadata.constraint_count SHALL equal: length(constraints)

Any mismatch SHALL invalidate the formalization.

=================================================
SYMBOL COVERAGE RULE
=================================================

Every symbol appearing in fol_formula SHALL:

- appear in fol_traceability.symbols
- appear in ast_constraints
- appear in variables
- appear in z3_signature

Every symbol appearing in ast_constraints SHALL:

- appear in fol_formula
- appear in variables
- appear in z3_signature

Partial symbol coverage is prohibited.

=================================================
FORMALIZABILITY RULE
=================================================

A requirement is FORMALIZABLE whenever at least one logical relation can be extracted.

The presence or absence of:

- shall
- must
- should
- may
- will
- expected
- target
- goal

SHALL NOT determine formalizability by itself.

Use logical structure only.

A requirement MAY be classified as: formalization_status = NOT_FORMALIZABLE

ONLY if ALL are true:

1. no actor identified
2. no action identified
3. no logical relation identified

If NOT_FORMALIZABLE:

formalization_reason MUST be one of:

- No actor identified
- No action identified
- No logical relation identified

=================================================
SEMANTIC LOSS DETECTION RULE
=================================================

Before finalizing formalization verify that no meaningful semantic element has been lost.

Examples:

- obligations
- constraints
- limits
- thresholds
- purposes
- qualifiers
- expectations
- quality attributes
- quantitative targets

If a semantic element is omitted:

formalization_status = FORMALIZABLE_WITH_INFORMATION_LOSS

formalization_reason = Semantic element omitted during extraction

=========================================
OUTPUT COMPLETENESS GATE
=========================================

processed_count SHALL equal length(requirements).

detected_requirement_count SHALL equal length(requirements)

If the counts differ, the output SHALL be considered invalid.

=================================================
OUTPUT COMPLETENESS FIREWALL
=================================================

Before returning output:

1. Count detected Requirement IDs.

2. Count requirement objects contained in: requirements

3. Verify:

   detected_requirement_count =
   processed_count =
   length(requirements)

4. Verify:

   formalizable_count +
   not_formalizable_count =
   processed_count

5. If ANY count differs:

   - output is invalid
   - regenerate requirements
   - regenerate summary statistics

6. The formalizer SHALL NOT return output while counts are inconsistent.

7. Every detected Requirement ID SHALL appear exactly once inside requirements.

8. Missing Requirement IDs are prohibited.

9. Duplicate Requirement IDs are prohibited.

=================================================
LARGE BATCH PROCESSING RULE
=================================================

Formalization SHALL be independent of batch size.

The formalizer SHALL behave identically for:

- 1 requirement
- 10 requirements
- 100 requirements
- 1000 requirements

Large batches SHALL NOT justify:

- omission of requirements
- summarization of requirements
- aggregation of requirements
- skipping requirements
- partial requirement arrays

Every detected Requirement ID SHALL generate exactly one requirement object.

Batch size SHALL NOT alter formalization behavior.

=================================================
FORMALIZATION PIPELINE
=================================================

For every FORMALIZABLE requirement generate:

1. domains
2. predicates
3. functions
4. constants
5. fol_formula
6. ast_constraints
7. variables
8. constraints
9. formalization_metadata

Traceability rules:

- every element must be traceable to the requirement
- no external knowledge may be introduced

Minimum rules:

If actor and action exist:

- at least one predicate is required

If fol_formula exists:

- ast_constraints MUST exist

If ast_constraints exists:

- variables MUST exist
- constraints MUST exist

=================================================
SINGULARITY PROTECTION RULE
=================================================

Logical decomposition is a modeling activity.

The existence of:

- multiple predicates
- multiple domains
- multiple variables
- multiple constraints
- conjunctions
- disjunctions

does NOT imply:

- multiple requirements
- multiple obligations
- a Singularity violation

Only the source requirement determines the number of obligations.

Only obligations explicitly appearing inside the current requirement may be considered when reasoning about obligation structure.

=================================================
FOL GENERATION
=================================================

Every FORMALIZABLE requirement SHALL generate at least one FOL formula.

The formula MUST preserve:

- actor
- action
- object
- condition
- purpose
- obligation semantics
- qualifiers
- quality attributes

Only NOT_FORMALIZABLE requirements may return an empty fol_formula.

=================================================
FOL SEMANTIC PRESERVATION RULE
=================================================

Goals, purposes, motivations, intended outcomes, and rationale SHALL NOT be modeled as independent obligations.

Example:

ProvideDocumentation(d)

PurposeOf(
    ProvideDocumentation(d),
    ReduceHelpDeskCalls
)

=================================================
AST-FOL EQUIVALENCE RULE
=================================================

For every FORMALIZABLE requirement:

fol_formula and ast_constraints SHALL represent
exactly the same logical semantics.

Neither representation may contain:

- symbols
- operators
- constraints
- conditions
- purposes
- qualifiers
- obligations

that are absent from the other representation.

AST SHALL be considered the authoritative machine-readable representation.

fol_formula SHALL be considered the human-readable representation of the same logical model.

Any mismatch between fol_formula and ast_constraints SHALL invalidate the formalization.

=================================================
SOLVER-READY Z3 MODELING
=================================================

The purpose of the generated Z3 model is to enable direct SMT-based logical consistency
analysis.

Every FORMALIZABLE requirement SHALL generate a solver-ready logical model.

The generated model SHALL explicitly contain:
- domains
- predicates
- functions
- constants
- variables
- constraints
- ast_constraints

Every symbol referenced in:

- fol_formula
- ast_constraints 
- constraints

MUST correspond to a declared logical element.

Undeclared symbols are prohibited.

=================================================
LOGICAL SIGNATURE RULE
=================================================

Every predicate appearing in:

- fol_formula
- ast_constraints
- constraints

SHALL be declared in z3_signature.predicates.

Every function appearing in:

- fol_formula
- ast_constraints
- constraints

SHALL be declared in z3_signature.functions.

Every constant appearing in:

- fol_formula
- ast_constraints
- constraints

SHALL be declared in z3_signature.constants.

Every variable appearing in:

- fol_formula
- ast_constraints
- constraints

SHALL be declared in variables.

Every symbol referenced in:

- fol_formula
- ast_constraints
- constraints

MUST exist in z3_signature.

Undeclared symbols are prohibited.

Variables SHALL reference only symbols explicitly used in:

- fol_formula
- ast_constraints

Unused variables are prohibited.

All logical elements SHALL remain traceable to the source requirement.

All logical elements SHALL preserve semantic equivalence with the source requirement.

The logical signature SHALL be sufficient to support direct translation of ast_constraints into solver-evaluable Z3 propositional expressions.


=================================================
AST GENERATION
=================================================

Every non-empty fol_formula SHALL generate a non-empty AST constraint model.

Logical constraints SHALL be represented as structured JSON trees.

The following node types are allowed:

- VAR
- CONST
- NOT
- AND
- OR
- IMPLIES
- IFF
- LT
- LE
- GT
- GE
- EQ
- NE

Node definitions:

VAR

{{
  "type": "VAR",
  "name": "ForwardCall"
}}

NOT

{{
  "type": "NOT",
  "operand": "<AST_NODE>"
}}

AND

{{
  "type": "AND",
  "operands": [...]
}}

OR

{{
  "type": "OR",
  "operands": [...]
}}

IMPLIES

{{
  "type": "IMPLIES",
  "antecedent": "<AST_NODE>",
 "consequent": "<AST_NODE>"
}}

IFF

{{
  "type": "IFF",
  "left": "<AST_NODE>",
  "right": "<AST_NODE>"
}}

Constraints SHALL be represented as AST structures only.

String-based logical expressions are prohibited.


=================================================
VARIABLES AND CONSTRAINTS
=================================================

variables SHALL contain only logical symbols explicitly
referenced in:

- fol_formula
- ast_constraints

Every variable SHALL:

- have a name
- have a source reference

Every variable SHALL appear in at least one:

- fol_formula
- ast_constraint

Unused variables are prohibited.

Variables SHALL correspond only to symbols that exist in:

- z3_signature.predicates
- z3_signature.constants

Undeclared variables are prohibited.

=================================================
PROPOSITIONAL LOGIC MODELING RULE
=================================================

The current formalization model uses propositional logic.

The following AST node types are supported:

- VAR
- CONST
- NOT
- AND
- OR
- IMPLIES
- IFF
- LT
- LE
- GT
- GE
- EQ
- NE
Quantifiers are not part of the current logical model.

The formalizer SHALL NOT generate:

- FORALL
- EXISTS
- universal quantification (∀)
- existential quantification (∃)

Predicates SHALL be represented as propositional symbols.

Predicates used in:

- fol_formula
- ast_constraints

SHALL be declared in:

- z3_signature.predicates

Only predicates with:

- arity = 0

are supported.

Example:

Predicate:

{{
  "name": "AuthenticatedUser",
  "arity": 0
}}

FOL:

AuthenticatedUser

AST:

{{
  "type": "VAR",
  "name": "AuthenticatedUser"
}}


Numeric operators SHALL use binary AST nodes.

Example:

{{
  "type": "LE",
  "left": {{
    "type": "VAR",
    "name": "ResponseTime"
  }},
  "right": {{
    "type": "CONST",
    "value": 2
  }}
}}

Every symbol appearing in:

- fol_formula
- ast_constraints

MUST exist in z3_signature.

Undeclared symbols are prohibited.

The generated AST SHALL remain directly translatable into solver-evaluable Z3 propositional expressions.

=================================================
CONSTRAINT COMPLETENESS RULE
=================================================

Every constraint SHALL reference at least one:

- predicate
- function
- constant

Constraints SHALL NOT contain undeclared symbols.

Constraints SHALL NOT be empty.

Every logical symbol used in a constraint SHALL exist in the logical signature.

=================================================
NUMERIC CONSTRAINT RULE
=================================================

If the requirement contains explicit numeric constraints such as:

- thresholds
- limits
- percentages
- counts
- measurements
- durations
- quantities

those values SHALL be preserved explicitly in the generated constraints.

Examples:

ResponseTime <= 2

Availability >= 99.9

SearchCount >= 1000

Numeric information SHALL NOT be omitted.

=================================================
QUALIFIER PRESERVATION IN CONSTRAINTS
=================================================

Qualifiers that affect requirement meaning SHALL remain visible in at least one:

- predicate
- function
- constraint

Examples:

- consistently
- ideally
- preferred
- target
- expected

Qualifiers SHALL remain traceable to the source requirement.

=================================================
SOLVER-READY VALIDATION RULE
=================================================

Before finalizing a requirement verify:

1. fol_formula exists.
2. ast_constraints exist.
3. variables exist.
4. constraints exist.
5. every variable is declared.
6. every variable appears in a constraint.
7. every predicate is declared.
8. every function is declared.
9. every constant is declared.
10. no undeclared symbol exists.
11. constraints are solver-evaluable.
12. numeric constraints are preserved.
13. qualifiers are preserved.
14. quality attributes are preserved.
15. semantic meaning is preserved.
16. every AST node type is valid.
17. every AST variable exists in z3_signature.
18. every AST variable is traceable to the requirement.
19. AST constraints are directly parsable by Z3.

If any validation fails:

solver_readiness = "UNKNOWN"

solver_readiness_explanation =
"The logical model contains insufficient information to evaluate satisfiability."

Otherwise:

solver_readiness = "READY_FOR_SOLVING"

=================================================
CONSISTENCY STATUS
=================================================

If:

- variables = []
OR
- constraints = []
OR
- no AST constraint model exists

Then:

solver_readiness = "UNKNOWN"

solver_readiness_explanation = "The logical model contains insufficient information to evaluate satisfiability."

Otherwise: solver_readiness = "READY_FOR_SOLVING"

UNKNOWN SHALL NOT be interpreted as:

- contradiction
- inconsistency
- UNSAT
- logical defect

=================================================
FORMALIZATION TYPE RULE
=================================================

formalization_metadata.formalization_type SHALL use
the same operator naming convention used by:

- fol_traceability.operator
- ast_constraints.type

Allowed values:

- VAR
- NOT
- AND
- OR
- IMPLIES
- IFF
- LT
- LE
- GT
- GE
- EQ
- NE

Values such as:

- IMPLICATION
- CONJUNCTION
- DISJUNCTION

are prohibited.

=================================================
FORMALIZATION COMPLETENESS CHECK
=================================================

The following chain MUST be preserved:

FORMALIZABLE
→ Predicates
→ FOL Formula
→ Z3 Expression
→ Variables
→ Constraints

=================================================
FINAL VALIDATION CHECK
=================================================

Verify:

1. No functionality introduced.
2. No business rules introduced.
3. No implementation decisions introduced.
4. No design decisions introduced.
5. No external knowledge introduced.
6. Source language preserved.
7. Every domain is traceable.
8. Every predicate is traceable.
9. Every function is traceable.
10. Every constant is traceable.
11. Every FOL symbol exists in the signature.
12. Every variable appears in a constraint.
13. Every requirement processed independently.
14. Reference resolution supported by evidence.
15. No external knowledge used.
16. Logical concepts generate predicates.
17. Non-empty FOL generates Z3.
18. Non-empty Z3 generates constraints.
19. Constraints exist whenever Z3 exists.
20. Qualifiers were preserved.
21. Quality attributes were preserved.
22. No semantic loss occurred.
23. No cross-requirement contamination exists.
24. Batch size did not affect formalization.
25. Output is valid JSON.

=================================================
FORMALIZATION SAFETY CHECK
=================================================

Verify:

1. Objects were not converted into actors.
2. Goals were not converted into obligations.
3. Purposes were not converted into constraints.
4. Logical decomposition did not create obligations.
5. Multiple predicates do not imply multiple obligations.
6. Multiple constraints do not imply multiple requirements.
7. Ambiguity was preserved.
8. No semantic defects were created.
9. No semantic violations were inferred.
10. Obligation structure matches the source.
11. Submission structure was not formalized.
12. Dataset structure was not formalized.
13. Formalization is independent of batch composition.
14. Quality attributes remain visible.
15. Qualifiers remain visible.
16. No semantic element was silently removed.

INPUT INTERPRETATION RULE

The input may contain:

- raw requirements
- requirement tables
- semantic validation reports
- requirement catalogs

Whenever a requirement statement is present, the formalizer SHALL create one requirement object.

Requirement statements SHALL NOT be ignored merely because they appear inside a report.

VALIDATION REPORT EXTRACTION RULE

If the input contains reports, tables, audit findings, semantic validation reports or review reports:

The formalizer SHALL extract requirements from:

- Requirement ID columns
- Original Requirement columns
- Requirement text fields

The formalizer SHALL ignore:

- findings
- recommendations
- verdicts
- observations
- reviewer comments

Only the original requirement text SHALL be formalized.

Only rows containing:

- Requirement ID
- Original Requirement

shall generate requirement objects.

Reviewer observations, improvement reports,
quality assessments and verdict summaries SHALL
NOT generate requirement objects.

==========================================
REQUIREMENT SOURCE SELECTION RULE
==========================================

When a table contains:

- Requirement ID
- Original Requirement
- Improvement Suggestion
- Improved Requirement
- Observation
- Verdict

The formalizer SHALL use ONLY:

Original Requirement

All other columns are informational and SHALL NOT be formalized.

=================================================
OUTPUT JSON STRUCTURE
=================================================

The root JSON object MUST be a JSON object.

The root JSON object SHALL NOT be a JSON array.

The root JSON object MUST contain:

{{
  "requirements": [],

  "fol_statistics": {{
    "requirements_with_fol": 0,
    "requirements_without_fol": 0,
    "implications": 0,
    "negations": 0,
    "conjunctions": 0,
    "disjunctions": 0,
    "equivalences": 0
  }},

  "formalization_summary": {{
    "detected_requirement_count": 0,
    "processed_count": 0,
    "formalizable_count": 0,
    "not_formalizable_count": 0,
    "formalization_performed": false
  }}
}}

requirements MUST be a JSON array.

Each formalized requirement SHALL be stored inside the requirements array.

Each requirement SHALL contain:

{{
  "requirement_id": "R0407",

  "source_requirement": "...",

  "normalized_requirement": "...",

  "formalization_status": "FORMALIZABLE",

  "formalization_reason": "",

  "formalization_metadata": {{
  "formalization_confidence": 95,
  "formalization_type": "IMPLICATION",
  "variable_count": 2,
  "constraint_count": 1
}},

  "actor": "...",

  "action": "...",

  "object": "...",

  "condition": "...",

  "purpose": "...",

  "obligation_level": "SHALL",

  "domains": [],

  "z3_signature": {{
    "sorts": [],

    "predicates": [
      {{
        "name": "BroadcastCall",
        "arity": 0,
        "source": "broadcast call"
      }},
      {{
        "name": "UserCanSpeak",
        "arity": 0,
        "source": "cannot speak"
      }}
    ],

    "functions": [],

    "constants": []
  }},

  "variables": [
    {{
      "name": "BroadcastCall",
      "type": "predicate",
      "source": "broadcast call"
    }},
    {{
      "name": "UserCanSpeak",
      "type": "predicate",
      "source": "cannot speak"
    }}
  ],

  "fol_formula":
    "BroadcastCall -> Not(UserCanSpeak)",
"fol_traceability": {{
  "symbols": [
    "BroadcastCall",
    "UserCanSpeak"
  ],
  "operator": "IMPLIES"
}},


  "ast_constraints": [
    {{
      "type": "IMPLIES",

      "antecedent": {{
        "type": "VAR",
        "name": "BroadcastCall"
      }},

      "consequent": {{
        "type": "NOT",

        "operand": {{
          "type": "VAR",
          "name": "UserCanSpeak"
        }}
      }}
    }}
  ],

  "constraints": [
    {{
      "constraint_id": "C1",

      "ast_ref": 0,

      "source":
        "broadcast call implies user cannot speak"
    }}
  ],

"solver_readiness": "READY_FOR_SOLVING",
"solver_readiness_explanation": ""
}}


=================================================
OUTPUT STRUCTURE CONSTRAINTS
=================================================

- The root object SHALL ALWAYS contain requirements.

- The root object SHALL ALWAYS contain formalization_summary.

- ast_constraints SHALL be used instead of ast_expression.

- String-based logical expressions used as executable constraints are prohibited.

- Every AST variable SHALL exist in z3_signature.

- Every AST variable SHALL be traceable to the requirement.

- Every variable SHALL contain:
  - name
  - type
  - source

- Every constraint SHALL reference at least one AST node.

- Every AST constraint SHALL be directly parsable by the Z3 engine.

- Every symbol used in fol_formula SHALL exist in z3_signature.

- Every symbol used in ast_constraints SHALL exist in z3_signature.

- formalization_metadata SHALL ALWAYS be present for FORMALIZABLE requirements.

- formalization_metadata.formalization_confidence SHALL be provided.

- formalization_metadata.variable_count SHALL equal the number of entries in variables.

- formalization_metadata.constraint_count SHALL equal the number of entries in constraints.

- ast_constraints SHALL contain only valid node types:
  - VAR
- CONST
- NOT
- AND
- OR
- IMPLIES
- IFF
- LT
- LE
- GT
- GE
- EQ
- NE

- Every AST node SHALL be recursively well-formed.

- Undeclared symbols are prohibited.

- Empty AST nodes are prohibited.

- Every constraint SHALL be solver-evaluable.

- Every FORMALIZABLE requirement SHALL generate:
  - z3_signature
  - fol_formula
  - ast_constraints
  - variables
  - constraints
  - formalization_metadata

- Every variable referenced in:
  - fol_formula
  - ast_constraints
  - constraints

  SHALL exist in:
  - variables
  - z3_signature.predicates
    OR
  - z3_signature.constants

- Every symbol referenced in:
  - fol_formula
  - ast_constraints
  - constraints

  SHALL be declared in z3_signature.

- NOT_FORMALIZABLE requirements MAY return:
  - empty ast_constraints
  - empty variables
  - empty constraints

- fol_formula and ast_constraints SHALL preserve the same logical meaning.

- AST generation SHALL preserve:
  - actors
  - actions
  - objects
  - conditions
  - purposes
  - qualifiers
  - quality attributes

  whenever present in the source requirement.

- The output SHALL remain compatible with direct parsing by the downstream Z3 AST parser.

=================================================
FINAL INSTRUCTION
=================================================

Return valid JSON only.

Do not return:

- explanations
- markdown
- code fences
- reasoning steps

=================================================
FORMALIZATION SELF-CHECK
=================================================

Before returning:

1. Count detected Requirement IDs.
2. Count objects in requirements.
3. The counts must be identical.
4. processed_count SHALL equal length(requirements).
5. formalizable_count + not_formalizable_count SHALL equal processed_count.
6. detected_requirement_count SHALL equal processed_count.
7. Every detected Requirement ID appears exactly once in requirements.
8. No Requirement ID is missing.
9. No Requirement ID appears more than once.
10. Every FORMALIZABLE requirement contains:
    - z3_signature
    - fol_formula
    - ast_constraints
    - variables
    - constraints
    - formalization_metadata
11. Every symbol referenced in:
    - fol_formula
    - ast_constraints
    - constraints exists in z3_signature.
12. Every variable exists in variables.
13. Every variable appears in:
    - fol_formula
    - ast_constraints
14. No undeclared symbols exist.
15. Ambiguity was preserved.
16. Qualifiers were preserved.
17. Quality attributes were preserved.
18. No external knowledge was introduced.
19. No cross-requirement contamination exists.
20. Output is valid JSON.
21. If any check fails, regenerate the output before returning.

Return structured JSON only.

from collections.abc import Generator
from typing import Any

import orjson
from fastapi.encoders import jsonable_encoder

from lfx.base.io.chat import ChatComponent
from lfx.helpers.data import safe_convert
from lfx.inputs.inputs import BoolInput, DropdownInput, HandleInput, MessageTextInput
from lfx.schema.data import Data
from lfx.schema.dataframe import DataFrame
from lfx.schema.message import Message
from lfx.schema.properties import Source
from lfx.template.field.base import Output
from lfx.utils.constants import (
    MESSAGE_SENDER_AI,
    MESSAGE_SENDER_NAME_AI,
    MESSAGE_SENDER_USER,
)


class ChatOutput(ChatComponent):
    display_name = "Chat Output"
    description = "Display a chat message in the Playground."
    documentation: str = "https://docs.langflow.org/chat-input-and-output"
    icon = "MessagesSquare"
    name = "ChatOutput"
    minimized = True

    inputs = [
        HandleInput(
            name="input_value",
            display_name="Inputs",
            info="Message to be passed as output.",
            input_types=["Data", "JSON", "DataFrame", "Table", "Message"],
            required=True,
        ),
        BoolInput(
            name="should_store_message",
            display_name="Store Messages",
            info="Store the message in the history.",
            value=True,
            advanced=True,
        ),
        DropdownInput(
            name="sender",
            display_name="Sender Type",
            options=[MESSAGE_SENDER_AI, MESSAGE_SENDER_USER],
            value=MESSAGE_SENDER_AI,
            advanced=True,
            info="Type of sender.",
        ),
        MessageTextInput(
            name="sender_name",
            display_name="Sender Name",
            info="Name of the sender.",
            value=MESSAGE_SENDER_NAME_AI,
            advanced=True,
        ),
        MessageTextInput(
            name="session_id",
            display_name="Session ID",
            info="The session ID of the chat. If empty, the current session ID parameter will be used.",
            advanced=True,
        ),
        MessageTextInput(
            name="context_id",
            display_name="Context ID",
            info="The context ID of the chat. Adds an extra layer to the local memory.",
            value="",
            advanced=True,
        ),
        MessageTextInput(
            name="data_template",
            display_name="Data Template",
            value="{text}",
            advanced=True,
            info="Template to convert Data to Text. If left empty, it will be dynamically set to the Data's text key.",
        ),
        BoolInput(
            name="clean_data",
            display_name="Basic Clean Data",
            value=True,
            advanced=True,
            info="Whether to clean data before converting to string.",
        ),
    ]
    outputs = [
        Output(
            display_name="Output Message",
            name="message",
            method="message_response",
        ),
    ]

    def _build_source(self, id_: str | None, display_name: str | None, source: str | None) -> Source:
        source_dict = {}
        if id_:
            source_dict["id"] = id_
        if display_name:
            source_dict["display_name"] = display_name
        if source:
            # Handle case where source is a ChatOpenAI object
            if hasattr(source, "model_name"):
                source_dict["source"] = source.model_name
            elif hasattr(source, "model"):
                source_dict["source"] = str(source.model)
            else:
                source_dict["source"] = str(source)
        return Source(**source_dict)

    async def message_response(self) -> Message:
        # First convert the input to string if needed
        text = self.convert_to_string()

        # Get source properties
        source, _, display_name, source_id = self.get_properties_from_source_component()

        # Create or use existing Message object
        if isinstance(self.input_value, Message) and not self.is_connected_to_chat_input():
            message = self.input_value
            # Update message properties
            message.text = text
            # Preserve existing session_id from the incoming message if it exists
            existing_session_id = message.session_id
        else:
            message = Message(text=text)
            existing_session_id = None

        # Set message properties
        message.sender = self.sender
        message.sender_name = self.sender_name
        # Preserve session_id from incoming message, or use component/graph session_id
        message.session_id = (
            self.session_id or existing_session_id or (self.graph.session_id if hasattr(self, "graph") else None) or ""
        )
        message.context_id = self.context_id
        message.flow_id = self.graph.flow_id if hasattr(self, "graph") else None
        message.properties.source = self._build_source(source_id, display_name, source)

        # Store message if needed
        if message.session_id and self.should_store_message:
            stored_message = await self.send_message(message)
            self.message.value = stored_message
            message = stored_message

        # Set accumulated token usage from all upstream LLM vertices.
        # This must happen AFTER send_message() because streaming captures
        # usage from chunks and would overwrite accumulated totals.
        if hasattr(self, "_vertex") and self._vertex is not None:
            accumulated_usage = self._vertex._accumulate_upstream_token_usage()  # noqa: SLF001
            if accumulated_usage:
                message.properties.usage = accumulated_usage
                if self.should_store_message and message.get_id():
                    message = await self._update_stored_message(message)
                    await self._send_message_event(message, id_=message.get_id())

        self.status = message
        return message

    def _serialize_data(self, data: Data) -> str:
        """Serialize Data object to JSON string."""
        # Convert data.data to JSON-serializable format
        serializable_data = jsonable_encoder(data.data)
        # Serialize with orjson, enabling pretty printing with indentation
        json_bytes = orjson.dumps(serializable_data, option=orjson.OPT_INDENT_2)
        # Convert bytes to string and wrap in Markdown code blocks
        return "```json\n" + json_bytes.decode("utf-8") + "\n```"

    def _validate_input(self) -> None:
        """Validate the input data and raise ValueError if invalid."""
        if self.input_value is None:
            msg = "Input data cannot be None"
            raise ValueError(msg)
        if isinstance(self.input_value, list) and not all(
            isinstance(item, Message | Data | DataFrame | str) for item in self.input_value
        ):
            invalid_types = [
                type(item).__name__
                for item in self.input_value
                if not isinstance(item, Message | Data | DataFrame | str)
            ]
            msg = f"Expected Data or DataFrame or Message or str, got {invalid_types}"
            raise TypeError(msg)
        if not isinstance(
            self.input_value,
            Message | Data | DataFrame | str | list | Generator | type(None),
        ):
            type_name = type(self.input_value).__name__
            msg = f"Expected Data or DataFrame or Message or str, Generator or None, got {type_name}"
            raise TypeError(msg)

    def convert_to_string(self) -> str | Generator[Any, None, None]:
        """Convert input data to string with proper error handling."""
        self._validate_input()
        if isinstance(self.input_value, list):
            clean_data: bool = getattr(self, "clean_data", False)
            return "\n".join([safe_convert(item, clean_data=clean_data) for item in self.input_value])
        if isinstance(self.input_value, Generator):
            return self.input_value
        return safe_convert(self.input_value)

"""Enhanced file component with Docling support and process isolation.

Notes:
-----
- ALL Docling parsing/export runs in a separate OS process to prevent memory
  growth and native library state from impacting the main Langflow process.
- Standard text/structured parsing continues to use existing BaseFileComponent
  utilities (and optional threading via `parallel_load_data`).

from __future__ import annotations

import contextlib

def _get_storage_location_options():

    if is_astra_cloud_environment():
        return all_options
    return [{"name": "Local", "icon": "hard-drive"}, *all_options]

    outputs = [
